minutes.headline: Planning Board reorganized with uncontested slates, endorsed an ANR, and continued a sign hearing for lack of an applicant.
minutes.summary: The board held its annual reorganization, filling officer and committee seats by uncontested nominations. It endorsed an ANR for 932 Flat Hill Road, continued the Lancaster Avenue sign hearing to July 8, and appointed Ann Lockwood to the open space committee. It also discussed the Sunny Hill Road rain garden completion, a master plan implementation committee, feedback to the Select Board on outdoor dining, and the water supply protection district draft.

public_comment.topic: Asked why the Pledge of Allegiance is not said during meetings and urged the chair to put it to a board vote.
Asked that the Zoom audio output be louder.

Water commissioner asked for copies of proposed water supply protection district changes, raised concern about treatment restrictions in zones one and two, and asked that the state agency review any changes.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board endorsed an ANR plan for 932 Flat Hill Road.
The board approved all uncontested nominees for its reorganization positions and the town manager screening committee.
The 3 Lancaster Avenue sign hearing was continued to July 8 at 6:05 p.m.
Ann Lockwood was appointed to the open space ad hoc committee as a citizen at large.
On the Sunny Hill Road rain gardens, the contractor is to send a written account of the corrections before a certificate of completion is considered.

why_it_matters: The Sunny Hill Road performance guarantee covers both lots and is not released until both are satisfied, so the town's protection on that development stays in place until the rain garden corrections are reviewed.

The board is also preparing written outdoor dining feedback for the Select Board and has a water supply protection district draft in progress, both of which could affect rules for local businesses and land near public water supplies.
watch_next: July 8: the Lancaster Avenue sign hearing resumes and the MBTA zoning presentation is rescheduled.
July 22: the public hearing on the 240 Summer Street site plan and stormwater.
